source_prompt:
# Instructions for accurately documenting structural defects in a bridge maintenance report

1. Start with the maintenance records.
2.
completion:
Thoroughly review all previous maintenance records, including past inspections, repairs, and any noted issues. Pay special attention to recurring problems as these may indicate systemic failures or design flaws.

3. Perform a visual inspection.
Conduct a comprehensive visual inspection of the bridge from multiple perspectives. This includes walking across the bridge, inspecting under it, and observing it from a distance. Look for visible signs of damage such as cracks, spalling, exposed rebar, rust, misalignments, tilted or displaced structural elements, and erosion under footings.

4. Document exterior defects.
Use a digital camera to take high-resolution photographs of any defects. Label each photo with the exact location, time, and date. Include scales or markers in the photos to provide context for the size and extent of the defect.

5. Document interior and hidden defects.
